notes.name-it-exactly:
Try together: When you are both calm, ask: “What feeling fits?” Listen. Then choose one small thing to try together.

Name it to tame it: Use your familiar reminder when a new hard moment comes along.

What research says: In some studies with adults, naming feelings helped people feel less upset. That does not tell us whether this story helps children.

Read more: Sources and study details are in the app. Torre and Lieberman, 2018.
notes.compare-with-past-me:
Try together: When you are both calm, try this together: Name one change: 'Then I read one page. Now I read three. Practice helped.'

Reminder: When a new hard moment comes along, use your familiar reminder: “Not their race. Grow at your pace.”.

What research says: Evidence type: Children, same skill. These sources do not tell us whether this story helps your child.

Read more: Sources and study details are in the app. Gürel and others, 2020.
notes.long-breath-out:
Try together: When you are both calm, try this together: Before the first test question, try three slow breaths out.

Reminder: When a new hard moment comes along, use your familiar reminder: “Breathe out slow, let it flow.”.

What research says: Evidence type: Children, same skill. These sources do not tell us whether this story helps your child.

Read more: Sources and study details are in the app. Kiat Hui Khng, 2017.
